question.text: Is the Retromandibular Transparotid Approach a Reliable Option for the Surgical Treatment of Condylar Fractures?
question.context: This study evaluated the outcomes and complications of the surgical treatment of condylar fractures by the retromandibular transparotid approach. The authors hypothesized that such an approach would be safe and reliable for the treatment of most condylar fractures. A retrospective evaluation of patients who underwent surgical reduction of a condylar fracture from January 2012 to December 2014 at the Clinic of Dentistry and Maxillofacial Surgery of the University Hospital of Verona (Verona, Italy) was performed. Inclusion criteria were having undergone surgical treatment of condylar fractures with a retromandibular transparotid approach and the availability of computed tomograms of the preoperative and postoperative facial skeleton with a minimum follow-up of 1 year. Static and dynamic occlusal function, temporomandibular joint health status, presence of neurologic impairments, and esthetic outcomes were evaluated in all patients. The sample was composed of 25 patients. Preinjury occlusion and temporomandibular joint health were restored in most patients. Esthetic outcomes were deemed satisfactory by clinicians and patients. Neither permanent neurologic impairments nor major postoperative complications were observed.

medgemma_4b.clinical_reasoning: The study evaluated the retromandibular transparotid approach for condylar fractures and found that it was safe and reliable, with no permanent neurologic impairments or major postoperative complications. The outcomes, including restoration of preinjury occlusion and temporomandibular joint health, and satisfactory esthetic results, support the use of this approach.
medgemma_4b.critical_evidence: Neither permanent neurologic impairments nor major postoperative complications were observed.
medgemma_4b.differential_considered: While the study focused on condylar fractures, other facial fractures might require different approaches. However, the study's focus and the absence of complications make the retromandibular transparotid approach a reliable option for condylar fractures as described in the case.

rnj1_8b.clinical_reasoning: The study demonstrates that the retromandibular transparotid approach is safe and effective for condylar fracture treatment, with 100% restoration of preinjury occlusion and TMJ health, satisfactory esthetic outcomes, and no permanent neurologic impairments or major complications. The large sample size of 25 patients and 1-year follow-up provide strong evidence for reliability.
rnj1_8b.critical_evidence: No permanent neurologic impairments or major postoperative complications were observed in any of the 25 patients
rnj1_8b.differential_considered: Alternative approaches like direct condylotomy or zygomatic approach were not compared in this study, but the lack of complications in this specific technique makes it a reliable option for most cases

qwen3_vl_8b.clinical_reasoning: The study demonstrated that the retromandibular transparotid approach achieved successful restoration of occlusion, TMJ health, and esthetic outcomes in most patients, with no permanent neurologic impairments or major complications. This supports the reliability of the approach for condylar fracture treatment.
qwen3_vl_8b.critical_evidence: No permanent neurologic impairments nor major postoperative complications were observed in the 25 patients studied.
qwen3_vl_8b.differential_considered: Alternative approaches (e.g., intraoral or transmandibular) were not evaluated in this study, so their comparative safety or efficacy cannot be assessed; however, the absence of complications in this cohort supports the reliability of this specific approach.

olmo3_7b.critical_evidence: Neither permanent neurologic impairments nor major postoperative complications were observed in the 25 patients followed for at least one year.
olmo3_7b.differential_considered: Other approaches (e.g., lateral, sagittal split, or sagittal fixation) may carry higher risks of complications or longer recovery times, but the presented data specifically demonstrate that the retromandibular transparotid approach was safe and effective in this cohort.
